title: The Minnal Murali Boys Are Back. Athiradi Brings Tovino Thomas and Basil Joseph to Your Screen This Friday.
excerpt: The ₹50-crore Malayalam campus entertainer hits SonyLIV on June 19 — in five languages — pitting a fest-reviving dreamer against a former goon who just wants to sing.
body:
Some movies are built for a packed theatre, and **Athiradi** is one of them — a Malayalam campus entertainer so loud, so crowd-pleasing, so engineered for collective whooping that it ran past ₹50 crore worldwide on the strength of word of mouth alone. The good news for everyone who missed its May theatrical run, or who lives a continent away from the nearest Malayalam screen: it lands on **SonyLIV** on June 19, and it's coming in five languages — Malayalam, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada and Hindi.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=syBtRf69q6s</youtube>

That multilingual drop matters. Malayalam cinema has spent the last two years quietly becoming the most exciting film industry in the country, and the diaspora has had to work to keep up — chasing subtitles, hunting down screenings, trading recommendations in group chats. A simultaneous five-language premiere on a major platform is exactly how a regional hit becomes a national, and then global, conversation.

The pairing alone is the selling point. **Tovino Thomas** and **Basil Joseph** — the two halves of the *Minnal Murali* magic — are back on screen together, and there's a reason that combination makes Malayali audiences sit up. Basil, who shot to fame as a director before becoming one of the industry's most lovable on-screen presences, plays Samkutty — Sam Boy — a civil engineering student brimming with so much manic energy he decides to single-handedly revive *Arohan*, his college's legendary cultural fest, which was banned years ago after a stampede.

Standing directly in his way is Tovino's Sreekuttan, and this is where the film finds its sly, beating heart. Sreekuttan is a former goon — "Thotta" Kuttan — who's been nursing one absurdly tender dream: to perform his song before a live audience. The fest that Sam wants to revive is the same event Sreekuttan once got banned. When the two ambitions collide, the film detonates into a battle of egos that's equal parts comedy, drama and large-scale action.

It's a deceptively simple setup — a fest, a feud, a former thug who just wants to sing — but debutant director **Arun Anirudhan** mines it for everything it's worth. The film leans hard into its campus setting, then keeps puncturing it with larger-than-life character beats, and the result is the kind of movie that resonated loudest with younger audiences who saw their own college chaos blown up to mass-movie scale.

Tovino, in particular, is having a moment. He has spent the last few years toggling between superhero spectacle, intense drama and exactly this sort of swaggering crowd-pleaser, and his Sreekuttan is reportedly one of his most purely entertaining turns — a thug with a karaoke dream is a gift of a role, and he plays it with full commitment. Basil, meanwhile, brings his trademark earnest-underdog charm, the everyman energy that has made him one of Malayalam cinema's most bankable nice guys.

The supporting bench is loaded with the kind of names that make Malayalam film fans smile in recognition — Vineeth Sreenivasan, Riya Shibu, Zarin Shihab, Shaan Rahman and Jeo Baby among them. Behind the camera, cinematographer Samuel Henry and music director Vishnu Vijay give the film its bright, festival-season energy; this is a movie that wants you tapping your foot, and it largely succeeds.

Produced by Dr. Ananthu S under Ananthu Entertainments alongside Basil Joseph Entertainments, *Athiradi* arrives on streaming roughly a month after its theatrical bow — a tight turnaround that speaks to SonyLIV's confidence in its rewatch appeal. And rewatch appeal is the whole point of a film like this. It's not built to win awards. It's built to be the thing you put on with family on a Friday night, the comfort-food entertainer that makes a Kerala college feel like home whether you're watching from Kochi, Toronto or New Jersey.

SonyLIV's own tagline for the premiere said it best: "The rivalry you didn't know you needed." For a diaspora hungry for the next Malayalam hit and a reason to gather around the screen, that's enough. Stream it from June 19 in the language of your choice — and settle in for two-and-a-half hours of pure, unbothered fun.
